# SMALL WILD NEIGHBOURS — editorial facts

## Book identity and readership

- Title: SMALL WILD NEIGHBOURS
- Subtitle: A nature notebook for English towns
- Cover age label: Ages 8–12
- Reading age: 8–12
- Language: English
- Geographic scope: English town parks and gardens
- Main outing season: spring to early autumn
- Outing duration and time: short daytime visits
- Companionship: an accompanying adult
- Subject set: European robin; Blue tit; Common daisy; White clover; 7-spot ladybird; Garden snail
- Encounter status: six possible subjects, with presence varying by place and visit
- Seasonal context: broader seasonal information retained in the species notes; photograph dates independent of the main outing season
- Identification scope: the six supplied subjects and their described features
- Evidence basis: supplied biological notes and their institutional source records
- Practice entry status: Practice example — not a field record
- Publisher mark, author biography, retail price, institutional logo and ISBN: unsupplied

## Illustration identity

- Medium and surface language: original observational ink-and-colour-wash illustration; visible ink strokes and translucent washes
- Composition basis: independently composed observations using the photographs for external appearance
- Treatment: simplified incidental texture; recognisable diagnostic natural colour patches and external structures
- Organism character: natural animal and plant anatomy and behaviour
- Depicted stages: adult birds, adult ladybird, garden snail and flowering plants
- Enlarged-feature label: Detail
- Scale relationship: individual natural views and enlarged details, with scale specific to each view
- Natural occlusion: partly hidden structures appropriate to the viewing angle
- Layout palette count: 3
- Layout palette: dark green #24352A; pale green #DCE5C9; rust #AD5B3C
- Organism palette: natural diagnostic colours described in 03-species-facts.en.md and supported by the appearance photographs

## Overview text pattern

- Name fields: exact common name and scientific name
- Fact statements per overview: 3 concise statements preserving the supplied meaning
- Feature labels per overview: at least 2, connected to the actual illustrated features
- Observation questions per overview: 1
- Reading style: readable English for ages 8–12
- Technical vocabulary: a plain-language definition beside first use
- Editable prose: fact statements and prompts, with their supplied meaning retained
- Fixed text: names, required headings and page numbers
- Fact coverage: a selection of supplied facts appropriate to each page
- Text and image relationship: matching feature, colour and structure descriptions

## Page geometry

- Single-page trim: 148 × 210 mm
- Facing spread: 296 × 210 mm; left page followed by right page
- Binding fold: centre of the facing spread
- Outer-edge margin: 6 mm
- Text, label and diagnostic-feature safe band: 6 mm on each side of the binding fold
- Background wash area: page field, including margin and fold bands
- Text columns: 2 per page
- Column gap: 4 mm
- Column width: 66 mm
- Page numbering: both assigned page numbers, one on each page
- Supplied editorial spread raster reference: 2368 × 1680 pixel PNG
- Supplied editorial front-cover raster reference: 1184 × 1680 pixel PNG
- Geometry status: nominal editorial page dimensions
- Manufacturing specification: unassigned

## Looking and recording

- Shared method: Pause → Notice → Record
- Observation setting: quiet observation with an accompanying adult from an accessible path or permitted garden
- Living subjects: plants rooted; animals in their existing positions; nests observed at a distance
- Activity scope: looking, listening, sketching and recording during daytime visits
- Record fields: place; date/time; weather; visible features; sketch; behaviour; uncertainty
- Observation field label: I noticed
- Question field label: I wonder
- Valid absence entry: Not seen
- Method distinction: observations recorded separately from questions and possible explanations
- Practice form heading: Practice example — not a field record
- Practice data source: 04-practice-record.md

## Navigation and page allocation

- Index heading: Find a neighbour
- Reserved page span: 2–41
- Chapter names: Observe and record; Birds; Flowers; Small animals
- European robin overview: 4–5
- Blue tit overview: 6–7
- Common daisy overview: 8–9
- White clover overview: 10–11
- 7-spot ladybird overview: 12–13
- Garden snail overview: 14–15
- Index page references: the same six overview page pairs in tiers 6, 14 and 24
- Active samples and reserved pages: 06-page-plan.md
- Spread unit: two facing pages counted as one artwork
- Detail and comparison unit: one spread, including its internal panels
- Catalog unit: one independently exported deliverable per row
- Film frames and presentation pages: components of their respective video and document
- Tier 6 scope: finished sample artworks
- Tiers 14 and 24 sequence: specification; cover, method and overview applications; index and recording applications; publication showcase and presentation
- Worked-form relationship: completion of the actual blank form
- Tier 24 extensions: named overview sources developed into feature details and comparisons; additional observation-method spreads
- Reuse basis: actual delivered book artworks in the film and presentation

## Appearance reference relationships

- Biological authority: 03-species-facts.en.md
- Appearance support: seven original photographs
- Individual and location relationship: separate photographs may show different individuals and locations
- Shared physical scale: unassigned
- ref-robin.jpg target: adult face/breast patch, brown back and pale belly
- ref-blue-tit.jpg target: adult cap, face stripe, wings and underparts
- ref-daisy.jpg target: white/yellow daisy heads
- ref-daisy.jpg companion content: unrelated blue flowers and background leaves
- ref-daisy-leaves.jpg target: rooted low rosette of spoon-shaped leaves
- ref-clover.jpg target: rounded pale flower heads and three-leaflet leaves
- ref-ladybird.jpg target: adult external form and visible spot arrangement
- ref-snail.jpg target: mottled coiled shell, body and tentacles
- Credits, licences, locations, dates and original-file records: 05-reference-credits.en.md
- Constraint image: field-notebook-geometry.png
- Atmosphere image: park-observation-scene.png

# Six subjects for English urban nature observation

- Text basis: concise biological facts paraphrased from the institutional sources listed below
- Application: English town parks and gardens
- Subject scope: the six supplied subjects
- Depicted stages: adult birds, adult beetle, snail and flowering plants
- Photograph role: external appearance
- Photograph locations: capture locations recorded separately from book observation settings
- Observation prompts: editorial questions for readers

## robin — European robin / Erithacus rubecula

- Adult appearance: orange-red face and breast, brown back and pale belly
- Adult sexes: males and females look alike
- Juvenile appearance: speckled brown, with the adult red breast developing later
- UK occurrence: parks, gardens and cities throughout the year
- Behaviour: frequent singing from a perch
- Linked recognition clues: adult face/breast patch, brown back and pale belly
- Illustration stage: adult
- Juvenile comparison medium: explanatory words
- Observation prompt: Watch from a distance. Where is the robin perched, and does it move before you finish one sketch?
- Fact sources: R1

## blue-tit — Blue tit / Cyanistes caeruleus

- Adult appearance: blue cap and wings, white face crossed by a dark eye stripe, greenish back and yellow underparts
- Beak: short and fine
- UK occurrence: widespread in parks, gardens, woodland and hedges
- Behaviour: clinging to feeding surfaces; joining mixed groups of tits in winter
- Linked recognition clues: distinct cap, eye stripe and yellow underparts
- Illustration stage and pose: adult resting on a twig
- Detail relationship: the same cap, eye stripe and underpart features as the adult overview
- Observation prompt: Notice the face first, then the body. Which two colour areas help you find the same bird again after it changes position?
- Fact sources: R2

## daisy — Common daisy / Bellis perennis

- UK occurrence: widespread in short grass, including lawns and parks
- Leaves: spoon-shaped, forming a low rosette
- Flower structure: a head containing many tiny flowers
- Centre: yellow disc florets
- Edge: white ray florets
- Flowering period: much of the year
- Illustration structure: rooted plant above the soil, low leaf rosette, slender flower stalk and white/yellow head
- Enlargement subject: the two kinds of tiny flowers
- Enlargement type: explanatory diagram
- Observation prompt: With the plant rooted, look at a flower head and then its leaves. Where do the leaves sit compared with the flower?
- Fact sources: P1

## clover — White clover / Trifolium repens

- UK occurrence: widespread in grassy places, including lawns and parks
- Usual leaf: three green leaflets, often with pale markings
- Leaf variation: exceptions to the usual three-leaflet pattern
- Flower heads: rounded, white and sometimes pinkish
- Common flowering period: May to October
- Flower visitors: bumblebees
- Illustration structure: one intact leaf with three leaflets joined at one point, beside a rounded flower head
- Pale markings: variable
- Observation prompt: Look at one leaf while leaving it attached. How many leaflets can you see clearly, and which part is hidden?
- Fact sources: P2

## ladybird — 7-spot ladybird / Coccinella septempunctata

- Adult wing cases: red with seven black spots
- Spot arrangement: three on each side and one shared spot near the front
- Thorax: black-and-white markings
- UK occurrence: widespread, including parks and gardens
- Food: aphids
- Common adult observation period: March to October
- Illustration views: adult from above or an oblique angle that communicates the seven-spot arrangement
- Natural occlusion: far-side spots may be hidden
- Complete-pattern view: explanatory top-view diagram
- Photograph role: adult external form
- Observation prompt: Count only the spots you can see. If a spot is hidden by the viewing angle, record that uncertainty while leaving the insect in place.
- Fact sources: I1, I2

## snail — Garden snail / Cornu aspersum

- UK occurrence: across the UK
- Shell: coiled; the animal can withdraw into it
- Land-snail head tentacles: usually two retractable pairs
- Eyes: carried on the upper pair
- Activity: often at night; also possible in wet daytime weather
- Shell and slime-trail evidence: an individual maker remains uncertain from these traces alone
- Appearance reference: mottled, coiled shell
- Illustration features: two long upper tentacles; lower tentacles may be small or hidden by the natural angle
- Body relationship: mollusc body carrying its attached shell
- Shell diameter and growth-age data: unsupplied
- Observation prompt: After rain, watch an animal already in view from the path. Which parts extend, and which parts remain inside the shell?
- Fact sources: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5

steps.userMessage:
SMALL WILD NEIGHBOURS | A children's field notebook for English town nature

We are developing an illustrated nature notebook for children aged 8–12 and their accompanying adults, for short daytime visits to English town parks and gardens from spring to early autumn. Print the title "SMALL WILD NEIGHBOURS", the subtitle "A nature notebook for English towns" and the age label "Ages 8–12" on the front cover. The six subjects are European robin, Blue tit, Common daisy, White clover, 7-spot ladybird and Garden snail. The shared page plan reserves pages 2–41; the samples listed below are supplied, and every index uses the same six overview page pairs.

The direction is original observational ink-and-colour-wash illustration, with visible ink strokes, translucent washes and recognisable natural colour patches and structures. Use three layout colours: dark green #24352A, pale green #DCE5C9 and rust #AD5B3C; organism colours follow the species facts and appearance photographs. Single pages measure 148 × 210 mm, with two text columns per page, a 4 mm column gap, 6 mm outer margins and a 6 mm text-and-feature safe band on each side of the binding fold. Each overview contains the exact common and scientific names, three short fact statements, at least two labels pointing to the illustrated features and one observation question. Use the method labels Pause, Notice and Record in that order. Recording pages use the exact labels I noticed, I wonder and Not seen; the index heading is "Find a neighbour". Observation takes place quietly with an adult, from an accessible path or permitted garden, with plants rooted and animals left where they are. Use the supplied practice record for the worked form, headed "Practice example — not a field record".

Audience: children and parents using the book outdoors, and our editorial and design teams deciding the page system and illustrated sample set for publication.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the editorial scope, fixed wording and page geometry. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md identifies every deliverable, its proportion, format and stage. 03-species-facts.en.md supplies the six subjects' biological facts, observation prompts and source records. 04-practice-record.md supplies the worked observation entry. 05-reference-credits.en.md records the appearance photographs' credits, dates, locations and licences. 06-page-plan.md fixes the chapters and page pairs. field-notebook-geometry.png is the constraint image for the trim, columns, margins and binding fold. ref-robin.jpg is an identity reference for the adult robin's face, breast, back and belly. ref-blue-tit.jpg is an identity reference for the adult blue tit's cap, face stripe, wings and underparts. ref-daisy.jpg is an identity reference for the white-and-yellow daisy heads. ref-daisy-leaves.jpg is an identity reference for the daisy's rooted leaf rosette. ref-clover.jpg is an identity reference for clover leaves and flower heads. ref-ladybird.jpg is an identity reference for the adult beetle's form and spot pattern. ref-snail.jpg is an identity reference for the snail's shell, body and tentacles. park-observation-scene.png is an atmosphere reference for a child and parent observing from a park path.

Deliverables:
1. One written layout and illustration specification, two pages, stating the title and subtitle, ages 8–12, three layout colour codes, page and grid measurements, actual typeface names, overview content pattern, six subjects' identifying features and recording labels
2. One front cover applying the specification, with the title, subtitle, age label and an original illustration of at least one supplied subject
3. Three illustrated method spreads: Pause, Notice and Record on pages 2–3; observation places on pages 32–33; and observation questions on pages 34–35
4. Fourteen illustrated species spreads: six overviews on pages 4–15; six corresponding feature-detail spreads on pages 16–27; a European robin and Blue tit comparison on pages 28–29; and a Common daisy and White clover comparison on pages 30–31
5. One species index spread on pages 36–37, with six common names, scientific names and overview page pairs
6. Two observation record spreads: a blank form on pages 38–39 and the same form completed with 04-practice-record.md on pages 40–41
7. One 10-second publication showcase video reusing the delivered cover, method spread, all six species overviews, one detail spread, both comparison spreads and blank-to-worked record sequence
8. One presentation document of at least twelve pages, reusing the specification, cover, three method spreads, fourteen species spreads, index and both record spreads

Acceptance:
- The specification comes first and states 148 × 210 mm, two columns per page, a 4 mm column gap, 6 mm outer margins and fold bands, ages 8–12, and #24352A, #DCE5C9 and #AD5B3C; the cover and page artworks apply these rules, and the presentation repeats these numbers and codes together with the actual typeface names.
- The cover and specification print SMALL WILD NEIGHBOURS and A nature notebook for English towns; the cover also prints Ages 8–12.
